title: GPU availability surface — weekly snapshot (2026-05-21)
content:
Purpose: weekly export of the ‘availability surface’ view used by infra and SRE to track true usable GPU capacity across clusters and pools (sample window: 2026-05-14 to 2026-05-20). This is an intermediate sheet-format export (derived from Grafana timeseries + pool scheduler logs).

Definitions / methodology:
- time window: 7-day rolling (Mon 2026-05-14 00:00 UTC to Sun 2026-05-20 23:59 UTC)
- avg_util: average active vcore-equivalent GPU utilization per pool (weighted by instance-hours)
- p95_util: 95th percentile instantaneous utilization across the window
- headroom_pct: fraction of pool capacity that was idle and immediately schedulable (accounting for fragmentation)
- wasted_slots: estimated percentage of slots that could not be used due to instance size mismatch or partial fragmentation
- data sources: grafana panel id: gpu-availability-surface, scheduler logs (slot-alloc events), capacity catalog

High level findings:
1) Fleet-level avg_util: 71% (weighted by GPU-seconds) with p95 at 91% during the 2026-05-18 afternoon surge. This is marginally up (+4ppt) vs the previous week.
2) Region breakouts: us-west1 remains the tightest (avg_util 82%, p95 96%), eu-west1 sits at 68% avg, apac-southeast1 at 62% avg but with highest fragmentation/wasted_slots.
3) Fragmentation spike: apac pools with mixed T4/RTX-share instances show ~16–20% wasted_slots during nights (local business hours for APAC customers cause fragmentation with long-running training jobs).
4) Emergent risk: cluster-alpha (us-west1) had two 30–45m windows where the scheduler reported <5% instantaneous idle but autoscaler failed to spin additional burst nodes due to quota throttling (see linked Linear ticket).
5) Reserve policy suggestion: add a 6% soft headroom target to us-west1 pools for next 2 weeks to reduce request latency for high-priority routes; implement gradual bump rather than instant commit.

Per-cluster quick snapshot (short bullets):
- cluster-alpha (us-west1): pools: a100-80, a100-40-burst. avg_util a100-80 = 88% (p95 97%), headroom 8%, wasted_slots 4%. Action: short-term reserve of 5% on a100-80 until May 31.
- cluster-beta (eu-west1): pools: v100-shared, a10g-lowprio. avg_util v100-shared = 64% (p95 85%), headroom 22%, wasted_slots 6%. Observation: good headroom but higher variance — run cleanup for stale reservations.
- cluster-kota (apac-southeast1): pools: t4-economy, rtx-6000-mixed. avg_util t4-economy = 59% (p95 78%), headroom 12%, wasted_slots 18%. Action: evaluate pool split by size to reduce fragmentation.

Anomalies of note:
- 2026-05-18 15:00–15:45 UTC: fleet p95 spike to 96% driven by model-run promotions in us-west1; surfaced by alerts gpu-p95-breach-uw1. Root cause: marketing-led internal evals routed to hosted capacity; mitigation: add routing tag to dev/eval traffic.
- 2026-05-16 02:00–03:20 UTC (apac): sudden uptick in wasted_slots correlated with backend patch that changed instance packing policy (PR #8342). Rollback reduced fragmentation by ~6ppt.

CSV export summary included below (rows sample; full dataset available on linked Grafana).

Notes and caveats:
- These numbers are export-derived and include best-effort correction for timezones and daylight savings; still expect small diffs vs live dashboards.
- ‘headroom’ here is immediate scheduling headroom and does not include ability to burst to dedicated capacity or spin new GCE nodes (those are handled by autoscaler logs separately).

Bottom-line recommendations (short):
- Add a temporary 6% soft reserve to us-west1 a100 pools for high-priority routes through next sprint.
- Run 'small-size' pool split for apac t4-economy to reduce wasted_slots and rerun cost/quality eval.
- Address autoscaler throttle errors for cluster-alpha with quota request + fallback policy patch (see Linear ENG-INFRA-742).
- Add tag-based routing for internal eval traffic to avoid saturating hosted capacity during peak windows.

Prepared by: Evan Rios (eng-infrastructure) — raw export attached as CSV below and pushed to Grafana snapshot.
action_items:
1) Evan: submit quota bump request for us-west1 (target: +10% burst capacity) — due 2026-05-26.
2) Aisha & Priya: prototype pool split for t4-economy in apac and run A/B evaluation on wasted_slots — due 2026-06-02.
3) Noah: add tag-based routing for internal/eval traffic in router rules, add exclude flag for hosted-slo-critical routes — due 2026-05-28.
4) SRE: monitor autoscaler throttle alerts (alert: autoscaler-throttle-uw1) and validate fallback policy is exercised in next simulated surge — due 2026-05-29.
notes: Export generated from Grafana snapshot 'gpu-availability-surface' and scheduler logs; this sheet is a working artifact intended for infra planning sync. If you need raw per-minute series, ping for the S3 export link.
